section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of a Single Transformation
section_1.content: Briefly review that a 2D matrix multiplication (A * v) represents a linear transformation. Visually demonstrate how a grid transforms when basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1) move to new coordinates. Introduce 'Momo the Robot' standing on the grid to show how his shape stretches or rotates.
section_1.example: Momo the Robot is scaled by factor 2 horizontally and 0.5 vertically. The matrix A = [[2, 0], [0, 0.5]] represents this single transformation.

section_2.title: The Sequential Challenge: Two Steps in a Row
section_2.content: Introduce the scenario where Momo needs to undergo two transformations sequentially. First, a 90-degree rotation (Transformation A), followed by a horizontal shear (Transformation B). Show the grid morphing twice in a sequence. Define the goal: Can we find a single 'Master Matrix' that does both at once?
section_2.example: Momo first rotates 90 degrees left, then gets pushed (sheared) to the right. We track his position after step 1, then apply step 2 to that new position.

section_3.title: Function Composition Logic (The 'Right-to-Left' Rule)
section_3.content: Explain that matrix multiplication works like function nesting: f(g(x)). If we apply transformation A first, then B, the math looks like B(A(v)). This explains why, in the product BA, the matrix representing the first action is written on the right.
section_3.example: Written as Vector_final = [Shear Matrix] * ([Rotation Matrix] * Vector_initial). The right-most matrix is the 'first responder'.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Composition via Basis Vectors
section_4.content: Demonstrate that the columns of the resulting matrix C (where C = BA) are simply the results of tracking where the original i-hat and j-hat end up after both transformations are applied. Use animation to follow the path of i-hat from (1,0) -> A(i-hat) -> B(A(i-hat)).
section_4.example: If A rotates i-hat to (0,1) and B shears (0,1) to (1,1), then the first column of the combined matrix C is (1,1).

section_5.title: Why Order Matters (Non-Commutativity)
section_5.content: Use a visual example to show that changing the order of matrices changes the result. This is a critical property of matrix multiplication. Rotate then Shear is not the same as Shear then Rotate.
section_5.example: Show Momo: (1) Rotating then (2) Shearing results in him leaning diagonally. (1) Shearing then (2) Rotating results in him leaning vertically. The visuals are distinct, proving AB ≠ BA.

section_6.title: Summary: The Computational Shortcut
section_6.content: Conclude that matrix multiplication is not just a bunch of dot products; it is the mathematical 'glue' that fuses multiple spatial actions into one. This allows computers to calculate complex 3D animations (like Momo jumping and spinning) using a single pre-calculated matrix.
section_6.example: In video games, a character's rotation, scaling, and movement are all multiplied into one 'Model Matrix' to render the frame efficiently.

section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of a Single Transformation
section_1.content: Briefly review that a 2D matrix multiplication (A * v) represents a linear transformation. Visually demonstrate how a grid transforms when basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1) move to new coordinates. Introduce 'Momo the Robot' standing on the grid to show how his shape stretches or rotates.
section_1.example: Momo the Robot is scaled by factor 2 horizontally and 0.5 vertically. The matrix A = [[2, 0], [0, 0.5]] represents this single transformation.

section_2.title: The Sequential Challenge: Two Steps in a Row
section_2.content: Introduce the scenario where Momo needs to undergo two transformations sequentially. First, a 90-degree rotation (Transformation A), followed by a horizontal shear (Transformation B). Show the grid morphing twice in a sequence. Define the goal: Can we find a single 'Master Matrix' that does both at once?
section_2.example: Momo first rotates 90 degrees left, then gets pushed (sheared) to the right. We track his position after step 1, then apply step 2 to that new position.

section_3.title: Function Composition Logic (The 'Right-to-Left' Rule)
section_3.content: Explain that matrix multiplication works like function nesting: f(g(x)). If we apply transformation A first, then B, the math looks like B(A(v)). This explains why, in the product BA, the matrix representing the first action is written on the right.
section_3.example: Written as Vector_final = [Shear Matrix] * ([Rotation Matrix] * Vector_initial). The right-most matrix is the 'first responder'.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Composition via Basis Vectors
section_4.content: Demonstrate that the columns of the resulting matrix C (where C = BA) are simply the results of tracking where the original i-hat and j-hat end up after both transformations are applied. Use animation to follow the path of i-hat from (1,0) -> A(i-hat) -> B(A(i-hat)).
section_4.example: If A rotates i-hat to (0,1) and B shears (0,1) to (1,1), then the first column of the combined matrix C is (1,1).

section_5.title: Why Order Matters (Non-Commutativity)
section_5.content: Use a visual example to show that changing the order of matrices changes the result. This is a critical property of matrix multiplication. Rotate then Shear is not the same as Shear then Rotate.
section_5.example: Show Momo: (1) Rotating then (2) Shearing results in him leaning diagonally. (1) Shearing then (2) Rotating results in him leaning vertically. The visuals are distinct, proving AB ≠ BA.

section_6.title: Summary: The Computational Shortcut
section_6.content: Conclude that matrix multiplication is not just a bunch of dot products; it is the mathematical 'glue' that fuses multiple spatial actions into one. This allows computers to calculate complex 3D animations (like Momo jumping and spinning) using a single pre-calculated matrix.
section_6.example: In video games, a character's rotation, scaling, and movement are all multiplied into one 'Model Matrix' to render the frame efficiently.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Sequential Challenge: Two Steps in a Row",
            [
                "- First, we rotate Momo 90 degrees counter-clockwise.",
                "- Next, we apply a horizontal shear to him.",
                "- Can we find one matrix for both steps?"
            ]
        )

        # Colors for consistency
        ROT_COLOR = "#58C4DD"  # Light blue
        SHEAR_COLOR = "#83C167"  # Light green
        MOMO_COLOR = "#FFD700"  # Gold/Yellow
        
        # Define Momo
        momo_body = Square(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.5, color=MOMO_COLOR)
        eye_l = Dot(point=[-0.2, 0.2, 0], color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        eye_r = Dot(point=[0.2, 0.2, 0], color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        smile = Arc(radius=0.2, start_angle=-TAU/4 - 0.5, angle=1, color=WHITE)
        momo = VGroup(momo_body, eye_l, eye_r, smile)
        
        # Define the coordinate system (NumberPlane)
        # We want it to stay within the right side area (A1 to F6)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": GREY,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            }
        )
        
        # Group Momo and Plane so they transform together
        transformation_group = VGroup(plane, momo)
        self.place_in_area(transformation_group, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Store original center for relative transformations
        group_center = transformation_group.get_center().copy()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ROT_COLOR)
        self.add(transformation_group)
        
        # Rotation Matrix (90 deg CCW)
        rot_matrix = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.apply_matrix(rot_matrix, about_point=group_center),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Revert first line color, highlight second
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SHEAR_COLOR)
        
        # Horizontal Shear Matrix (k=1)
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=group_center),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Revert second line color, highlight third
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Final emphasis - maybe a pulse or just showing the final result clearly
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.scale(1.1),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.scale(1/1.1),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's compare two different sequences of transformations.",
            "Rotate then Shear creates one spatial result.",
            "Shearing then rotating produces a different outcome.",
            "Notice the distinct shapes Momo takes.",
            "This proves that matrix multiplication order matters."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper to create "Momo" as a composite VMobject
        def create_momo(color=BLUE):
            body = Square(side_length=1, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5)
            # Create eyes and mouth that are parts of the same group to transform together
            eye_l = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + LEFT*0.2 + UP*0.2)
            eye_r = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + RIGHT*0.2 + UP*0.2)
            smile = Arc(radius=0.2, start_angle=-PI*0.9, angle=PI*0.8, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + DOWN*0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        label_2 = Text("Scenario 2: Shear -> Rotate", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)

        self.place_at_grid(label_2, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        momo2 = create_momo(YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(momo1, "C2", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(momo2, "C5", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Sequence 1: Rotate then Shear

        self.play(momo1.animate.rotate(90*DEGREES, about_point=momo1.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        # Shear along X axis with factor 1
        self.play(momo1.animate.shear(1, X_AXIS, about_point=momo1.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        )

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching titles and lines from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Composition via Basis Vectors"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Trace i-hat's path through the first transformation.",
            "Follow its journey through the second step.",
            "These final coordinates become our first column.",
            "Repeat this entire process for j-hat.",
            "The combined matrix is now complete."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"  # Red for i-hat
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"  # Green for j-hat
        
        # Create Coordinate System
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C3", "F6")
        self.add(plane)
        
        # Create Matrix C structure
        # Matrix C = [[?, ?], [?, ?]]
        matrix_label = MathTex("C = ", font_size=32)
        bracket_l = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix}", font_size=40)
        bracket_r = MathTex(r"\end{bmatrix}", font_size=40)
        
        entry_11 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        entry_21 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        entry_12 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        entry_22 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        
        col1 = VGroup(entry_11, entry_21).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        col2 = VGroup(entry_12, entry_22).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        entries = VGroup(col1, col2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        matrix_group = VGroup(matrix_label, bracket_l, entries, bracket_r).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_group, "A3", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Basis vector labels above matrix
        label_i = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=COLOR_I, font_size=24).next_to(col1, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_j = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=COLOR_J, font_size=24).next_to(col2, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.add(matrix_group, label_i, label_j)
        
        # Define vectors
        # Helper to get position on plane
        def p(x, y): return plane.coords_to_point(x, y)
        
        vec_i = Vector([1, 0], color=COLOR_I)
        vec_i.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(1,0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Trace i-hat's path through the first transformation.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_I))
        self.play(Create(vec_i))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transformation A: i-hat (1,0) -> (0,1)
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(0,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Follow its journey through the second step.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_I))
        
        # Transformation B: i-hat (0,1) -> (1,1)
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(1,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # These final coordinates become our first column.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        res11 = MathTex("1", color=COLOR_I, font_size=32).move_to(entry_11)
        res21 = MathTex("1", color=COLOR_I, font_size=32).move_to(entry_21)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(entry_11, res11),
            Transform(entry_21, res21)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Repeat this entire process for j-hat.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_J))
        
        vec_j = Vector([0, 1], color=COLOR_J)
        vec_j.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(0,1))
        
        self.play(Create(vec_j))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transformation A: j-hat (0,1) -> (-1,0)
        self.play(
            vec_j.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(-1,0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transformation B: j-hat (-1,0) -> (-1,0)
        # Indicate that it stays there
        self.play(
            Indicate(vec_j, scale_factor=1.2, color=COLOR_J),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The combined matrix is now complete.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        res12 = MathTex("-1", color=COLOR_J, font_size=32).move_to(entry_12)
        res22 = MathTex("0", color=COLOR_J, font_size=32).move_to(entry_22)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(entry_12, res12),
            Transform(entry_22, res22)
        )
        
        # Box the matrix
        box = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_group, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the specific title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Computational Shortcut", [
            "Matrix multiplication fuses multiple actions into one.",
            "This efficiency powers modern 3D computer graphics.",
            "Composition turns sequences into a single calculation."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line and introduce matrices
        line1_color = BLUE_B
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(line1_color))
        
        # Create Matrices A, B, C and their labels
        # A = Shear, B = Rotation, C = Scaling
        mat_a = Matrix([["1", "1"], ["0", "1"]], color=line1_color)
        mat_b = Matrix([["0", "-1"], ["1", "0"]], color=line1_color)
        mat_c = Matrix([["2", "0"], ["0", "2"]], color=line1_color)
        mat_m = Matrix([["0", "-2"], ["2", "2"]], color=line1_color) # Result of C * B * A
        
        self.place_at_grid(mat_a, "B1", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(mat_b, "B2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(mat_c, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        lbl_a = MathTex("A", color=line1_color)
        lbl_b = MathTex("B", color=line1_color)
        lbl_c = MathTex("C", color=line1_color)
        lbl_m = MathTex("M", color=line1_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(lbl_a, "A1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(lbl_b, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(lbl_c, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(mat_a), FadeIn(lbl_a),
            FadeIn(mat_b), FadeIn(lbl_b),
            FadeIn(mat_c), FadeIn(lbl_c)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Merge matrices A, B, and C into one final matrix M at B2
        self.place_at_grid(mat_m, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(lbl_m, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(mat_a, mat_b, mat_c), mat_m),
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(lbl_a, lbl_b, lbl_c), lbl_m),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition highlight to second line
        line2_color = GREEN_B
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(line2_color)
        )
        
        # Create Momo (stick figure)
        momo_head = Circle(radius=0.2, color=line2_color)
        momo_body = Line(momo_head.get_bottom(), momo_head.get_bottom() + DOWN * 0.5, color=line2_color)
        momo_l_arm = Line(momo_body.get_center(), momo_body.get_center() + LEFT * 0.3 + UP * 0.1, color=line2_color)
        momo_r_arm = Line(momo_body.get_center(), momo_body.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.3 + UP * 0.1, color=line2_color)
        momo_l_leg = Line(momo_body.get_end(), momo_body.get_end() + LEFT * 0.2 + DOWN * 0.3, color=line2_color)
        momo_r_leg = Line(momo_body.get_end(), momo_body.get_end() + RIGHT * 0.2 + DOWN * 0.3, color=line2_color)
        momo = VGroup(momo_head, momo_body, momo_l_arm, momo_r_arm, momo_l_leg, momo_r_leg)
        
        self.place_at_grid(momo, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(momo))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Momo performing a complex jump and spin
        self.play(
            momo.animate.shift(UP * 1.0).rotate(2 * PI),
            rate_func=ease_out_sine,
            run_time=0.7
        )
        self.play(
            momo.animate.shift(DOWN * 1.0).rotate(2 * PI),
            rate_func=ease_in_sine,
            run_time=0.7
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight to third line and show conclusion
        line3_color = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(line3_color)
        )
        
        final_text = Text("Matrix Multiplication = Composition", font_size=24, color=line3_color)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "F2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(3)

        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # x from 0.5 to 5.5, y from 2.2 to -2.8
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section 1 Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Geometry of a Single Transformation"
        lines = [
            "A matrix transformation moves vectors in 2D space.",
            "Meet Momo the Robot, standing on our grid.",
            "We apply this matrix to the entire space.",
            "Watch Momo stretch as the grid morphs.",
            "Notice where the basis vectors land."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        i_color = "#FF0000"
        j_color = "#00FF00"
        momo_color = "#88C0D0"
        matrix_color = "#FFFF00"
        grid_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A matrix transformation moves vectors in 2D space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        # Display Matrix A at the top
        matrix_a = MathTex("A = \\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\\\ 0 & 0.5 \\end{bmatrix}", color=matrix_color)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_a, 'A3', 'A4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(matrix_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Meet Momo the Robot, standing on our grid.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        # Coordinate system (White grid)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": grid_color, "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=i_color, stroke_width=5)
        j_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(0,1), buff=0, color=j_color, stroke_width=5)
        i_label = MathTex("\\hat{i}", color=i_color, font_size=24).next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex("\\hat{j}", color=j_color, font_size=24).next_to(j_hat.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        # Momo the Robot (stick figure)
        # We'll create him relative to the screen origin first, then move him to the plane origin
        unit_len = np.linalg.norm(plane.c2p(1,0) - plane.c2p(0,0))
        
        head = Circle(radius=0.15 * unit_len, color=momo_color)
        body = Line([0, -0.15 * unit_len, 0], [0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        l_arm = Line([0, -0.3 * unit_len, 0], [-0.25 * unit_len, -0.25 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        r_arm = Line([0, -0.3 * unit_len, 0], [0.25 * unit_len, -0.25 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        l_leg = Line([0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], [-0.15 * unit_len, -0.9 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        r_leg = Line([0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], [0.15 * unit_len, -0.9 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        momo = VGroup(head, body, l_arm, r_arm, l_leg, r_leg)
        
        # Position Momo so his feet are at the origin of the plane
        momo.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)

        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.play(Create(momo))
        self.wait(1)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching titles and lines from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Composition via Basis Vectors"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Trace i-hat's path through the first transformation.",
            "Follow its journey through the second step.",
            "These final coordinates become our first column.",
            "Repeat this entire process for j-hat.",
            "The combined matrix is now complete."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"  # Red for i-hat
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"  # Green for j-hat
        
        # Create Coordinate System
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C3", "F6")
        self.add(plane)
        
        # Create Matrix C structure
        # Matrix C = [[?, ?], [?, ?]]
        matrix_label = MathTex("C = ", font_size=32)
        bracket_l = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix}", font_size=40)
        bracket_r = MathTex(r"\end{bmatrix}", font_size=40)
        
        entry_11 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        entry_21 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        entry_12 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        entry_22 = MathTex("?", font_size=32)
        
        col1 = VGroup(entry_11, entry_21).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        col2 = VGroup(entry_12, entry_22).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        entries = VGroup(col1, col2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        matrix_group = VGroup(matrix_label, bracket_l, entries, bracket_r).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_group, "A3", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Basis vector labels above matrix
        label_i = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=COLOR_I, font_size=24).next_to(col1, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_j = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=COLOR_J, font_size=24).next_to(col2, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.add(matrix_group, label_i, label_j)
        
        # Define vectors
        # Helper to get position on plane
        def p(x, y): return plane.coords_to_point(x, y)
        
        vec_i = Vector([1, 0], color=COLOR_I)
        vec_i.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(1,0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Trace i-hat's path through the first transformation.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_I))
        self.play(Create(vec_i))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transformation A: i-hat (1,0) -> (0,1)
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(0,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Follow its journey through the second step.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_I))
        
        # Transformation B: i-hat (0,1) -> (1,1)
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(1,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # These final coordinates become our first column.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        res11 = MathTex("1", color=COLOR_I, font_size=32).move_to(entry_11)
        res21 = MathTex("1", color=COLOR_I, font_size=32).move_to(entry_21)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(entry_11, res11),
            Transform(entry_21, res21)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Repeat this entire process for j-hat.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_J))
        
        vec_j = Vector([0, 1], color=COLOR_J)
        vec_j.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(0,1))
        
        self.play(Create(vec_j))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transformation A: j-hat (0,1) -> (-1,0)
        self.play(
            vec_j.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(-1,0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transformation B: j-hat (-1,0) -> (-1,0)
        # Indicate that it stays there
        self.play(
            Indicate(vec_j, scale_factor=1.2, color=COLOR_J),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The combined matrix is now complete.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        res12 = MathTex("-1", color=COLOR_J, font_size=32).move_to(entry_12)
        res22 = MathTex("0", color=COLOR_J, font_size=32).move_to(entry_22)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(entry_12, res12),
            Transform(entry_22, res22)
        )
        
        # Box the matrix
        box = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_group, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

            "Shearing then rotating produces a different outcome.",
            "Notice the distinct shapes Momo takes.",
            "This proves that matrix multiplication order matters."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper to create "Momo" as a composite VMobject
        def create_momo(color=BLUE):

            eye_l = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + LEFT*0.2 + UP*0.2)
            eye_r = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + RIGHT*0.2 + UP*0.2)
            smile = Arc(radius=0.2, start_angle=-PI*0.9, angle=PI*0.8, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + DOWN*0.2)

        # Shear along X axis with factor 1

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Highlight both final states to show they are different
        box1 = SurroundingRectangle(momo1, color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        box2 = SurroundingRectangle(momo2, color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(box1), Create(box2))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(box1), FadeOut(box2))

        # This proves that matrix multiplication order matters.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF0000") # Red color for emphasis
        
        # Math inequality AB != BA
        inequality = MathTex("A", "B", "\\neq", "B", "A", font_size=48, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_in_area(inequality, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(momo1), FadeOut(momo2),
            FadeOut(label_1), FadeOut(label_2),
            Write(inequality)
        )
        
        # Flash the inequality to conclude the lesson on non-commutativity
        self.play(Flash(inequality, color="#FF0000", line_length=0.4, flash_radius=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section 1 Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Geometry of a Single Transformation"
        lines = [
            "A matrix transformation moves vectors in 2D space.",
            "Meet Momo the Robot, standing on our grid.",
            "We apply this matrix to the entire space.",
            "Watch Momo stretch as the grid morphs.",
            "Notice where the basis vectors land."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        i_color = "#FF0000"
        j_color = "#00FF00"
        momo_color = "#88C0D0"
        matrix_color = "#FFFF00"
        grid_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A matrix transformation moves vectors in 2D space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        # Display Matrix A at the top
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        matrix_a = Text("A = [[2, 0], [0, 0.5]]", color=matrix_color)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_a, 'A3', 'A4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(matrix_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Meet Momo the Robot, standing on our grid.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        # Coordinate system (White grid)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": grid_color, "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=i_color, stroke_width=5)
        j_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(0,1), buff=0, color=j_color, stroke_width=5)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_label = Text("i", color=i_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", color=j_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(j_hat.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        # Momo the Robot (stick figure)
        unit_len = np.linalg.norm(plane.c2p(1,0) - plane.c2p(0,0))
        
        head = Circle(radius=0.15 * unit_len, color=momo_color)
        body = Line([0, -0.15 * unit_len, 0], [0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        l_arm = Line([0, -0.3 * unit_len, 0], [-0.25 * unit_len, -0.25 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        r_arm = Line([0, -0.3 * unit_len, 0], [0.25 * unit_len, -0.25 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Metadata
        title = "Why Order Matters (Non-Commutativity)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's compare two different sequences of transformations.",
            "Rotate then Shear creates one spatial result.",
            "Shearing then rotating produces a different outcome.",
            "Notice the distinct shapes Momo takes.",
            "This proves that matrix multiplication order matters."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper to create "Momo" as a composite VMobject
        def create_momo(color=BLUE):
            body = Square(side_length=1, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5)
            # Create eyes and mouth that are parts of the same group to transform together
            eye_l = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + LEFT*0.2 + UP*0.2)
            eye_r = Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + RIGHT*0.2 + UP*0.2)
            smile = Arc(radius=0.2, start_angle=-PI*0.9, angle=PI*0.8, color=WHITE).move_to(body.get_center() + DOWN*0.2)
            return VGroup(body, eye_l, eye_r, smile)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's compare two different sequences of transformations.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        label_1 = Text("Scenario 1: Rotate -> Shear", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        label_2 = Text("Scenario 2: Shear -> Rotate", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_1, "A2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_2, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        momo1 = create_momo(BLUE)
        momo2 = create_momo(YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(momo1, "C2", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(momo2, "C5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label_1), FadeIn(label_2), FadeIn(momo1), FadeIn(momo2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rotate then Shear creates one spatial result.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Matrix for shearing along X axis with factor 1
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
        
        # Sequence 1: Rotate then Shear
        # Rotate 90 degrees CCW
        self.play(momo1.animate.rotate(90*DEGREES, about_point=momo1.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        # Shear along X axis with factor 1 using apply_matrix
        self.play(momo1.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=momo1.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Shearing then rotating produces a different outcome.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Sequence 2: Shear then Rotate
        # Shear along X axis with factor 1 using apply_matrix
        self.play(momo2.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=momo2.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        # Rotate 90 degrees CCW
        self.play(momo2.animate.rotate(90*DEGREES, about_point=momo2.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Notice the distinct shapes Momo takes.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Highlight both final states to show they are different
        box1 = SurroundingRectangle(momo1, color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        box2 = SurroundingRectangle(momo2, color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(box1), Create(box2))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(box1), FadeOut(box2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This proves that matrix multiplication order matters.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF0000") # Red color for emphasis
        
        # Math inequality AB != BA (Using Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex')
        inequality = Text("AB ≠ BA", font_size=48, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_in_area(inequality, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(momo1), FadeOut(momo2),
            FadeOut(label_1), FadeOut(label_2),
            Write(inequality)
        )
        
        # Flash the inequality to conclude the lesson on non-commutativity
        self.play(Flash(inequality, color="#FF0000", line_length=0.4, flash_radius=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    """
    Expert implementation of Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations.
    This scene demonstrates how applying matrix A followed by matrix B is equivalent 
    to applying the product matrix BA.
    """
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout (Title and Text content)
        title = Text("Matrix Multiplication as Composition", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        lecture_points = VGroup(
            Text("- Start with vector v", font_size=22),
            Text("- Apply Matrix A (Rotation)", font_size=22),
            Text("- Apply Matrix B (Scaling)", font_size=22),
            Text("- Result: T(v) = (B \u00b7 A) v", font_size=22)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        lecture_points.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)

        # 2. Setup Coordinate System (Right Side)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        origin = plane.coords_to_point(0, 0)
        
        # 3. Define the Vector
        # Initial vector v = [1, 1]
        v_coords = np.array([1, 1, 0])
        v_pointer = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(1, 1) - origin, color=YELLOW).shift(origin)
        v_label = Text("v", color=YELLOW, font_size=24).next_to(v_pointer.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # 4. Define Transformations (3x3 for Manim compatibility)
        # Matrix A: 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation
        matrix_a = [[0, -1, 0], 
                    [1,  0, 0], 
                    [0,  0, 1]]
        
        # Matrix B: Scaling x by 2
        matrix_b = [[2, 0, 0], 
                    [0, 1, 0], 
                    [0, 0, 1]]

        # 5. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 1: Initial Vector
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[0]))
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(v_pointer), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 2: Apply Transformation A
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[1]))
        self.play(
            v_pointer.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_a, about_point=origin),
            v_label.animate.move_to(plane.coords_to_point(-1.2, 1.2)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 3: Apply Transformation B
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[2]))
        # Note: apply_matrix applies relative to current state
        self.play(
            v_pointer.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_b, about_point=origin),
            v_label.animate.move_to(plane.coords_to_point(-2.2, 1.2)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 4: Conclusion
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[3]))
        
        # Highlight the final result
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(lecture_points[3], color=BLUE, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(Indicate(v_pointer, color=BLUE))
        
        self.wait(3)

        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        )
        
        # Highlight the completed matrix
        box = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_content, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8  # Adjusted for 6 columns on the right
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_str = "Summary: The Computational Shortcut"
        lines = [
            "Matrix multiplication fuses multiple actions into one.",
            "This efficiency powers modern 3D computer graphics.",
            "Composition turns sequences into a single calculation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)

        # Define Colors
        color_fuses = "#87CEEB"  # Sky Blue
        color_graphics = "#98FB98"  # Pale Green
        color_composition = "#FFD700"  # Gold

        # Asset Paths
        robot_path = "/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Matrix multiplication fuses multiple actions into one."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_fuses))

        # Matrices A, B, C
        matrix_a = MathTex("A", color=color_fuses)
        matrix_b = MathTex("B", color=color_fuses)
        matrix_c = MathTex("C", color=color_fuses)
        
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_b, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_c, "B3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a), FadeIn(matrix_b), FadeIn(matrix_c))
        self.wait(1)

        # Merge into Matrix M
        matrix_m = MathTex("M = C \\cdot B \\cdot A", color=color_fuses)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_m, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(matrix_a, matrix_b, matrix_c), matrix_m),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "This efficiency powers modern 3D computer graphics."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_graphics))

        # Coordinate Grid (Addressing Issue 39)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3, y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C2", "E5")
        
        # Momo (Robot Asset)
        try:
            momo = SVGMobject(robot_path).set_color(color_graphics)
        except:
            momo = Circle(color=color_graphics, fill_opacity=0.5).add(Text("Momo", font_size=12))
        
        self.place_in_area(momo, "C2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), FadeIn(momo))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Jump and Spin using Matrix M logic
        # We simulate the "fused action" with a single animation
        self.play(
            momo.animate.shift(UP * 0.5).rotate(2 * PI),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.play(
            momo.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.5),
            run_time=0.5,
            rate_func=bounce_it
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Composition turns sequences into a single calculation."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_composition))

        # Final Summary Text
        summary_text = Text("Matrix Multiplication = Composition", color=color_composition, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, "F1", "F6")

        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        
        # Indicate the final matrix and the text (Addressing Issue 40/41 style)
        self.play(
            Indicate(matrix_m, color=color_composition),
            Indicate(summary_text, scale_factor=1.1)
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
